sonnet.problem: The right answer ('Israel took what was devoted to destruction') was already told on the opening card of stop 1 ('acted unfaithfully regarding the things devoted to destruction... took some of what was set apart'). The baker can pick it without reasoning from this stop, and the card re-asks a fact already given.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. ... An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact.

sonnet.problem: The question asks what will be burned along with the man. That is the details of the violent punishment itself, not the choices or results around it.
sonnet.rule: Choice cards ask about the choices and results around them, never the act itself.

sonnet.problem: This card tells the discovery of Achan's hidden stolen goods, which is serious sin and leads straight into his death. It has a joke comparing it to Papa Dorin's years in the junk drawer ('hidden things get found'). The comparison also doesn't match: the drawer left him forgotten, while Achan hid things on purpose.
sonnet.rule: A card that tells death, violence, abuse, serious sin or the body's private matters has no joke.
